newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - May 20.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - May 20.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet and Brand-name Products.
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
PARIS - Publicis says its turnover rose six percent to 5.18 billion francs ($905.4 million) in the first quarter of 1997, largely due to expansion abroad. (Reuter)
PARIS - RMC and Sud Communication are putting together the fine details of the merger. They still have to negotiate agreements for their advertising space units. (La Tribune)

LONDON - Excite Inc says it launches European editions of its Internet search engines which will extend the reach of the Excite network, increase functionality and meet specific advertising requirements. Local products are launched in Britain, France, Germany and Sweden. (Reuter)

PARIS - Jacqueline Aglietta, chairman of French audience measurement body Mediametrie, defends TV viewing figures published by Mediametrie. Its figures have recently come under fire in a debate on audience numbers which is now widening to include the content of French TV programmes. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

PARIS - Turnover at publisher Filipacchi Medias rose to 375.1 million francs in the first quarter from 373.0 million in 1996's first three months, the company says. Magazine and advertising turnover fell in the period. (Reuter)
PARIS - Newly-launched French weekly news magazine Marianne's first few issues put it above breakeven, but its competitors have not so far suffered from its arrival. (La Tribune).
PARIS - French film industry watcher Centre National de la Cinematographie's most recent study says film production has shown a sharp recovery in Britain, Germany and Spain. (Les Echos)

CANNES - Cannes festival-goers wonder aloud why the film festival's 50th edition was made up of so many uninspiring films reeking of violence and evil. The jury rescued the jamboree with awards for a quirky Japanese film, "The Eel" by Shohei Imamura, and by flagging its support for two directors who have tussled with censors. (Reuter)
BRAND NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
PARIS - Dairy farmers blocked deliveries to hypermarkets in various parts of France in a protest against falling milk prices, unions say. (Reuter)
LONDON - French authorities may question the planned merger between British drinks giants Guinness and Grand Metropolitan, the Independent newspaper says. (Reuter)

PARIS - French drinks brand Orangina, a unit of Pernod Ricard, has begun delivering its fizzy orange drink in plastic screw-top bottles in France in a bid to target younger consumers, an Orangina spokeswoman says. (Reuter)
Paris Editorial, Sue Landau
For further information and news, see Reuters Advertising & Media Briefing. And visit us on the Internet at http://www.Bizinfo.reuters.com
